clue.text: Model animal — one to imitate

parts.note: to model something on another is to copy it
a cat is a common animal

explanation.surface: A model creature presented as the one everyone should follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A copycat is someone who mimics others, so this is a person you might choose to imitate, read loosely.

clue.text: Fighter in Burma found wounded in ditch

indicators.note: wounded means damaged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier from the Burma campaign is discovered injured in a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chindits were British-led special forces fighting behind Japanese lines in Burma during the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Chindits were members of the long-range penetration force in wartime Burma.

clue.text: Kiss, then show disdain — the hypocrite!

parts.note: a peck is a quick kiss
to sniff is to show contempt

explanation.surface: A kiss followed by a sneer exposes a two-faced person.
explanation.walkthrough: Seth Pecksniff is the oily hypocrite in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecksniff is the Dickens character whose name stands for sanctimonious insincerity.

clue.text: Rare object is strange but not useless

indicators.note: not tells us the abbreviation for useless is removed

parts.note: curious means strange
u/s, short for unserviceable, means useless

explanation.surface: An unusual item is odd but still has some use.
explanation.walkthrough: US is u/s, British services shorthand for unserviceable, i.e. broken or useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is an unusual collectable trinket, prized for rarity.

clue.text: Worker and master at work

indicators.note: at work means busy being reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A labourer and his boss on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is a skilled manual worker such as a plumber.

clue.text: Gives money' to get fuel — peat, perhaps

parts.note: to sub someone is to lend or advance them money
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Someone hands over cash to buy fuel, maybe peat for the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peat, perhaps' marks an example: peat can lie beneath the topsoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Peat is one kind of material found in the layer under the topsoil, so it is an example.

clue.text: Tobacco in tin used up

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
out means exhausted, used up

explanation.surface: The tobacco in the tin has all been smoked.
explanation.walkthrough: Snout is British prison slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: In prison slang snout means cigarettes or loose smoking leaf.

clue.text: Slaughter makes the line drop

parts.note: blood means lineage or family line
to shed is to drop

explanation.surface: A massacre causes the front line to fall back.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodshed is killing, especially in war.

clue.text: In the window, see Loire flowing

indicators.note: flowing like a river suggests the letters run into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Through the window you can watch the Loire run by.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a projecting bay window on an upper floor.

clue.text: Three articles bringing oblivion

parts.note: le is the French definite article
the English definite article
the English indefinite article before a vowel

explanation.surface: Three pieces of writing that make you forget everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The articles here are grammatical: one French, two English. Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethean describes forgetfulness, from the mythical underworld river whose waters wipe memory.

clue.text: Incorrigible — not able to earn

indicators.note: not tells us the word able is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: incorrigible means incurable, beyond correction
taken as written

explanation.surface: An incorrigible person is unable to earn a living.
explanation.walkthrough: You earn (or bring on yourself) blame in the same sense that you take it on.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn disapproval is to bring it on yourself, the sense of taking on a cost or penalty.

clue.text: One goal-post damaged by defender

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
taken as written

explanation.surface: A defender in football smashes into a goalpost and damages it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges I plus GOALPOST. The football defender is a false trail: here it is someone who argues in defence of a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist argues in support of a belief or person, a verbal champion.

clue.text: Stunner has one side tooth initially crooked

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
taken as written
S is short for side

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of the word tooth is used

explanation.surface: A beautiful person with one crooked tooth at the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' looks like it describes the tooth; it is the definition, meaning untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked here means corrupt, untruthful and deceitful.

clue.text: Patent in model vehicle may break new ground

indicators.note: patent means openly visible, so the letters lie plainly in sight within the next words

explanation.surface: A patent on a model vehicle could be a breakthrough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' looks like a noun (an invention's patent); it signals that the answer sits in plain view inside 'model vehicle'.
explanation.definitionFit: To break new ground is to dig, literally, and digging into earth is exactly that.

clue.text: Stupid to be very friendly

explanation.surface: Being foolish and being very close pals.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull-witted is one sense; 'thick as thieves' gives the other, intimate friendship.

clue.text: Raised flag by the way

parts.note: not a banner hoisted but a raised flagstone edging the roadway

explanation.surface: A flag hoisted beside the road, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner and 'by the way' like an aside; read flag as flagstone and way as road.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerbstones are the raised stones lining the pavement edge along a road.

clue.text: Malformed girl by chance having only half a heart

parts.note: miss is a girl or young woman

indicators.note: the heart of the word for chance is a doubled letter, and having only half of it leaves a single one

parts.note: to chance is to happen, as in it so chanced

explanation.surface: A girl born deformed, by bad luck, with only half her heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of HAPPEN is PP; 'having only half a heart' keeps one P.
explanation.definitionFit: Misshapen means twisted out of its normal form, a synonym of malformed.

clue.text: In the van, an asparagus tip

definitions.meaning: at the forefront, leading an attack
the pointed end of an asparagus shoot

explanation.surface: The tip of an asparagus spear riding in a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading the vanguard is one sense; the pointed top of an asparagus spear is the other.

clue.text: Meanness is an average sort of offence in the church

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
simony is the sin of buying or selling church offices

explanation.surface: Stinginess counts as a middling kind of church sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimony is extreme thrift, a reluctance to spend.

clue.text: Judge conceals first signs of neurotic character

annotationWithheld.why: Judge conceals first signs of neurotic character (9): REFEREE around NC needs 'character' for C, but 'character' is also the only definition, so one word does two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Judge conceals first signs of neurotic character

clue.text: Refuse to give destructive criticism

definitions.meaning: a noun here, meaning waste or garbage

explanation.surface: Declining to offer harsh comments.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun is waste; to slate something harshly is the verb sense.

clue.text: Keen to have free replacement at front of roof-top

indicators.note: replacement says the opening letters of the word for roof-top are changed for a new arrangement of them

parts.note: the ridge is the top line of a roof
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Someone eager for a free replacement at the front of the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The front of RIDGE is RID (free), rearranged as DIR. 'Keen' is not eager here but the noun for a wailing lament.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen is an Irish funeral lament, and a dirge is a mournful song for the dead.

clue.text: Promised to be busy

explanation.surface: Committed to being occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrothed to marry is one sense; occupied, as a phone line, is the other.

clue.text: Hotel worker is useful

definitions.meaning: a hotel servant who polished guests' shoes
the old verb boot, to avail

explanation.surface: A hotel employee who earns his keep.
explanation.definitionFit: A boots was a hotel servant who cleaned shoes; to boot, now archaic, means to be of use or avail.

clue.text: Beer may be readily available

definitions.meaning: drawn from a cask rather than a bottle

explanation.surface: Draught beer is handy whenever wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Draught beer is served from a cask; the phrase also means ready to use whenever needed.

clue.text: Punishment may be over-hasty in fact

indicators.note: in puts the word for over-hasty inside the word for fact

parts.note: a thing is a fact or matter
rash means over-hasty

explanation.surface: A punishment that was in fact handed down too hastily.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrashing is a beating, a physical penalty.

clue.text: Sees the sights in the Loire valley

definitions.meaning: a French city on the river Loire

explanation.surface: Sightseeing in the Loire region.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling round visiting places is one sense; a cathedral city on the Loire is the other.

clue.text: Take ship round the pole; it makes slow progress

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the voyage word goes around the pole

parts.note: to take ship is to set sail
N, the north pole

explanation.surface: Sail around the pole, a voyage that crawls along.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is a mollusc proverbial for its sluggish pace.

clue.text: Damaging reduction in blood

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harmful drop in the blood count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blood' is a verb here: to blood a newcomer is to give them a first taste of an activity.
explanation.definitionFit: To blood a recruit is to initiate them, bringing them into something for the first time.

clue.text: In company, half capital is invested in silver

indicators.note: invested in means wrapped inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: half says only the first half of the word for capital is kept

parts.note: London is the UK capital

explanation.surface: Half a company's capital is put into silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Along with means accompanying, together with someone.

clue.text: Unlucky Nazi shut in a place

indicators.note: shut in means enclosed, so the pieces go inside the Nazi's name

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy

explanation.surface: An unfortunate Nazi locked up in some place.
explanation.walkthrough: Hess was imprisoned for life at Spandau, which the surface recalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Hapless means unfortunate, having no luck.

clue.text: Filling in legal document, non expert got behind

indicators.note: filling something in means putting material inside it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
lay means non-professional, not expert

explanation.surface: An amateur filling in a legal form fell behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Delayed means held up, made late or fallen behind schedule.
